clue.text: Restrain pet that's also about to be caged

indicators.note: being caged means being shut inside, so the sulk encloses the other two pieces

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, a huff
also means and
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone tries to restrain a pet that is about to be put in a cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' looks like an animal but is the old word for a sulk; 'to be caged' puts AND and C inside HUFF.
explanation.definitionFit: To shackle someone's wrists is a way of restraining them, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Book hotel, mainly when one leaves for a resort

parts.note: H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means sort again, so the remaining letters are rearranged
one leaving means the letter for one goes out of the word mainly

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone books a hotel, mostly when one person leaves for a holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when one leaves' drops I from MAINLY, leaving MANLY; 'resort' (re-sort) shuffles that into YMNAL after H. 'resort' looks like a holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of hymns used in church is a specific kind of book.

clue.text: Almost votes against, admitting worry, in minority as before

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the trimmed vote word holds the pestering word
almost means not quite all, so the plural of no loses its last letter

parts.note: noes are votes against
to nag is to worry or pester

explanation.surface: Nearly all vote against, conceding worry about minority rights as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts NOES to NOE; 'admitting' puts NAG inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The old word for legal infancy, being under age, so a minority in the archaic sense.

clue.text: Building fat up — first ounce perhaps he's put on

parts.note: the ounce is the snow leopard, an example of a big cat
he is taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, so the fat word is backwards

parts.note: lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: Someone builds up their fat, and puts on another ounce first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ounce' looks like a weight but is the snow leopard; 'up' reverses LARD in this down clue, and 'first' puts CAT at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is a large church building, so it is an example of a building.

clue.text: Blow a cornet perhaps bought a long time ago

definitions.text: a cornet perhaps bought a long time ago
definitions.meaning: an ice-cream cone, a cornet, once cost fourpence in old British money

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a punch, and an ice cream bought long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: A cornet here is the British word for an ice-cream cone; fourpence was pre-decimal British money.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase for a clout or punch, and literally an item that cost fourpence.

clue.text: Lad full of impudence is easy to cope with when dressing

definitions.text: easy to cope with when dressing

indicators.note: a thing full of another holds it inside, so the son contains the cheek

parts.note: a lad is a son
lip is cheeky talk, impudence

explanation.surface: A cheeky boy is nonetheless easy to manage when getting him dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' puts LIP inside SON.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment with no fastenings, pulled straight on, is easy to manage when putting clothes on.

clue.text: Possibly writing short letter at first, in cruise vessel

indicators.note: at first means placed in front, so the note comes before the other piece

parts.note: drop me a line means send a short letter
writing is one of the three Rs, so R can stand for it

explanation.surface: A writer possibly dashes off a short letter on board a cruise ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so an R may be writing; 'at first' puts LINE before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean liner is a large passenger ship, which is what a cruise vessel is.

clue.text: One creating stimulus to pin down new cure

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top, pinning the second beneath it

parts.note: a prod is a stimulus or nudge

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the word cure is rearranged

explanation.surface: A nudge is needed to pin down a new remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns CURE into UCER; 'to pin down' sits PROD above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A producer makes or creates something, such as a film, a show or goods.

clue.text: There's no help in sight for it

definitions.text: There's no help in sight for it

parts.words: There's no help in sight for it
parts.note: sounds like a hopeless situation, but means vision with no aid such as a telescope or glasses

explanation.surface: A gloomy verdict that the situation is hopeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no help in sight' reads as 'hopeless'; literally it is sight without any optical aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaided vision, without lenses, is said to be seeing with this phrase.

clue.text: Bully-boy who grew fed up with people

definitions.text: Bully-boy who grew fed up with people

parts.words: Bully-boy who grew fed up with people
parts.note: a bully-boy reads as a creature half bull and half man, and 'fed up with people' as nourished on human victims, as in the Cretan myth

explanation.surface: A thug became thoroughly sick of everyone around him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bully-boy' and 'fed up' look like a thug who is weary of others; read literally they are a bull-man raised on a diet of youths sent from Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cretan monster of myth had a bull's head on a man's body and ate human tribute.

clue.text: Where a pawn is temporarily sacrificed?

definitions.text: Where a pawn is temporarily sacrificed?

parts.words: Where a pawn is temporarily sacrificed?
parts.note: chess talk for a gambit, but read as an item handed over to a pawnbroker for a time, until it is redeemed

explanation.surface: A chess question about where one gives up a pawn for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture misleads: the pawn is something pawned, left with a pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods pawned are held by the pawnbroker until bought back, which is the idiom's literal sense.

clue.text: Love to be involved with sabotage to hunt here, at the last minute

indicators.note: being involved in sabotage means being wrecked, so these letters are scrambled together

explanation.surface: Activists plan to sabotage a hunt here at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be involved with sabotage' shuffles LOVE with HUNT HERE, twelve letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for the latest possible moment, just before a deadline.

clue.text: Corner member of tribe

definitions.meaning: a corner is where two lines meet at an ...
one of the Germanic people who settled England, alongside the Saxons and Jutes

explanation.surface: A tribesman is backed into a corner.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the space between meeting lines, as in a corner, and one of a Germanic tribe.

clue.text: Recover influence — drinks for everyone!

parts.note: pull is influence, clout
a round is a set of drinks bought for the whole group

explanation.surface: Someone gets their clout back and celebrates by buying drinks for the whole pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To come through an illness is to get better, a phrasal verb synonym for recovering.

clue.text: Point I missed — text goes into cunning way this solution is written

indicators.note: something missed is left out, here the letter I from the word for aiming

parts.note: to point a gun is to train it
taken as written

indicators.note: one thing going into another sits inside it, so the passage sits within the cunning word

parts.note: sly means cunning
verse is a passage of text, as in a Bible verse

explanation.surface: A pupil misses a point when a passage turns up within a puzzle-maker's clever way of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed' takes I out of TRAIN, giving TRAN; 'goes into' puts VERSE inside SLY. The definition refers to the entry itself, written across the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an across entry, so it is written crosswise, at right angles to the down answers.

clue.text: Getting cross about particular political issues?

definitions.text: Getting cross about particular political issues?

parts.words: Getting cross about particular political issues?
parts.note: sounds like losing one's temper over politics, but the cross is the mark a voter puts on a ballot paper about a single question

explanation.surface: Someone gets angry about certain political matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like anger; it is the voter's X on a ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Public votes on single questions are decided by crosses on ballot papers, plural of the Latin term.

clue.text: One only wanted to retain research facility that may be cut off

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: wanting to retain something means keeping hold of it, so the word for only holds the laboratory

parts.note: sole means only
a lab is a laboratory for research

explanation.surface: One person alone wanted to keep a research facility that might be closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanted to retain' puts LAB inside SOLE, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be isolated may be separated or cut off from the rest.

clue.text: Doctor noticed fillet's to be served

parts.note: saw means noticed
fillets means bones, as a cook bones a fish

explanation.surface: A doctor noticed that the fish fillet is about to be served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fillet's' reads as a possessive noun but is the verb 'fillets', meaning removes the bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawbones is old slang for a surgeon or doctor, from the days of amputation.

clue.text: Dirk perhaps chasing Oliver's partner? One could be very cutting

indicators.note: something chasing another comes after it, so the blade follows the comedian

parts.note: Oliver Hardy's comedy partner was Stanley (Stan) Laurel
a dirk is a Scottish dagger, an example of a knife

explanation.surface: A man called Dirk pursues Oliver's partner, which sounds rather cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dirk' looks like a man's name but is a dagger; 'chasing' puts KNIFE after STANLEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A retractable-bladed craft tool used for cutting, so it could indeed be very sharp.

clue.text: Problem with fitting in dance was over

parts.note: a jig is a lively dance

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word was is written backwards

explanation.surface: A dance was over, a problem with fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses WAS to SAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw puzzle is a problem solved by fitting pieces together.

clue.text: Here, opera house presented English poet's recital

indicators.note: a recital is something spoken aloud, so the poet's name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Sir Philip Sidney was an English Elizabethan poet

explanation.surface: An opera house staged a recital of an English poet's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recital' says the poet SIDNEY is spoken; it sounds like the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous opera house with the sail roofs stands on Sydney harbour in Australia.

clue.text: Reluctant to have brainy eccentric replacing old home for 9

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so the reluctant word holds the shuffled letters
the new letters replacing the old one means the letter for old is first removed

parts.note: loth, a variant spelling of loath, means reluctant

indicators.note: an eccentric is odd and off-centre, signalling the word brainy rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to have a clever odd character swap their old home for another.
explanation.walkthrough: LOTH is a spelling of loath. 'replacing old' takes O out of it; 'to have' puts ABYRIN, the anagram of BRAINY from 'eccentric', inside. 9 is the Minotaur, kept in a maze in Crete.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minotaur of 9 across was imprisoned in the maze built by Daedalus at Knossos.

clue.text: Looking back where troubadours have contributed?

indicators.note: the two words contribute some of their letters, which run on from one into the next

explanation.surface: A question about where medieval minstrels made their contribution, looking back.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'wheRE TROubadours', signalled by 'have contributed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro style deliberately imitates the past, so it is looking back.

clue.text: Favoured having bit of sunshine about, but it's wet

indicators.note: about means around, so the sunbeam goes round the popular word

parts.note: a ray is a single beam of sunlight
in means favoured or popular, as in the in crowd

explanation.surface: Something is favoured for having a little sun, but it turns out to be wet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts RAY around IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather with lots of showers is wet, so the adjective fits the phrase that describes it.

clue.text: Fish with egg? Show disapproval about that

indicators.note: about means around, so the jeer goes round the louse egg

parts.note: to boo is to show disapproval
a nit is the egg of a louse

explanation.surface: Fish served with egg prompts a diner to show disapproval about that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg' looks like a side dish for the fish but is a nit; 'about' puts BOO around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonito is a tuna-like fish of the mackerel family, so it is a specific kind of fish.

clue.text: Suspect business may be successful before long, missing nothing

parts.note: a going concern is one that is doing well, so going suggests successful

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the word for before long loses its letter for zero

parts.note: soon means before long
O is the shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A dubious venture may soon pay off, though nothing comes of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes one O (nothing) out of SOON, giving SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Shady or suspicious goings-on is an idiom for questionable activities or business.

clue.text: Refrain from taking action about railway station

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the phrase for not suing is read backwards

parts.note: to refrain from taking legal action is not to sue

explanation.surface: Someone holds back from acting with regard to a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking action' means legal action here: NOT SUE, turned 'about', gives the London terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Euston is one of the main London railway terminals, so it is an example of a station.

clue.text: At some stages, American 7 will be here

definitions.text: At some stages, American 7 will be here

parts.words: At some stages, American 7 will be here
parts.note: 7 down gives producer; stages are theatres, so this is the New York street where American impresarios put on shows

explanation.surface: An American creator will be present at several points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At some stages' suggests 'at certain points in time', but the stages are theatre stages; 7 is PRODUCER.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York theatre district is where American stage producers mount their big shows.
